irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01, Borrowing Base clause (b)(ii): "85% multiplied by the Net Orderly Liquidation Value percentage identified in the most recent Inventory appraisal ordered by the Administrative Agent"
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A percentage multiplier whose numeric value is not fixed by the contract but is instead set from time to time by an external, periodically-updated source (a third-party inventory appraisal) - distinct both from a fixed PERCENT literal and from a dollar-valued METRIC_REFERENCE.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: PERCENT requires a literal fractional value known at drafting time; METRIC_REFERENCE defaults to a MONEY valueType (or RATIO if explicitly marked) and has no 'externally-sourced, periodically reset percentage' semantics, so composing MULTIPLY(PERCENT, METRIC_REFERENCE, METRIC_REFERENCE) here understates that the middle operand is itself variable and extrinsically determined.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: An EXTRINSIC_PERCENT_REFERENCE (or a 'sourceBasis' attribute on METRIC_REFERENCE) node type to represent a percentage whose value is fixed by a designated external determination (e.g., 'most recent appraisal ordered by the Administrative Agent') rather than by the contract text itself.

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01, Payment Conditions clause (c) and its Restricted-Payment carve-out (certificate delivery/content requirements tied to Sections 5.03(a)(ii)/(b)/(a))
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A purely procedural/documentary precondition (a certificate must be delivered, in a specified form, certifying specified matters, with a possible agency waiver of one sub-requirement) that is not itself a financial or ratio test but is nonetheless a real, material gating condition.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: COMPARE/AND/OR/NOT operate on boolean-valued financial propositions; there is no primitive for 'a specified document must be delivered/contain specified certifications,' so such requirements can only be captured via UNSUPPORTED, losing their procedural structure (who delivers, to whom, in what form, with what discretionary waiver).
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: A DOCUMENTARY_CONDITION primitive (party, recipient, requiredContent[], waivable: boolean/gatedBy) to represent certification/delivery preconditions as first-class, structured nodes rather than free-text UNSUPPORTED escapes.
